sources: MONDAY Oct 19 2026 EARLY RUN (06:20 UTC, before the US open; US cash markets last closed Friday Oct 16, so every official US close is Friday, while oil, metals and FX carry live Monday Asia-session quotes). HEADLINE: THE OIL SHOCK HAS STARTED TO UNWIND. Trump signed an executive order over the weekend waiving the Graham Act sanctions and tariffs on Russian energy exports, and Iran put a Strait of Hormuz reopening deal on the table saying the strait could be open in under a week if Washington accepts. Brent fell about 1.8-2.2 pct to 107.86 USD/Bbl in Asian trading from the Friday settle of 109.86, with WTI quoted between 97.43 and 100.4 depending on source. That is the first material downward move in Brent in this episode and it attacks the single biggest driver on this board. Caveats: the move is only about 2 USD off a four-month high, Brent is still up roughly 3 pct on the week and roughly 30 pct above pre-war levels, and the bearish headlines are offsetting fresh bullish supply news rather than replacing it - an oil tanker hit a naval mine and exploded in the southern Strait of Hormuz on Sunday per the IRGC navy (unverified), Hormuz disruption has cut HSFO bunker flows by about 800k tons with refinery attacks cutting another 1M tons, and Trump himself cited Ukrainian strikes on Russian diesel refineries as the reason for the waiver. So this is a policy-driven easing of a supply shock that is still physically live. Trend still up on the week, but the direction of travel changed this morning. NO OTHER MARKET TILE HAS NEW DATA - the five risk tiles are Friday closes carried unchanged: VIX 21.41, MOVE 101.10, curve 0.35, breakevens 2.33, HY OAS 323. WHAT THE OFFICIAL SOURCES CONFIRM THIS MORNING: FRED T10Y2Y Oct 16 0.35 (0.33 Oct 15, 0.37 Oct 14, 0.42 Oct 13) - the curve is at the flattest of this episode, down about 9bp on the week, but it steepened 2bp on the Friday rout. FRED T5YIFR Oct 16 2.33 (2.31 Oct 15, 2.34 Oct 14, 2.33 Oct 13) - long-run inflation expectations are flat on the week despite 3.7 pct headline CPI and a 110 USD oil touch. This remains the most important tile on the board and it is still saying the market believes the Fed. FRED BAMLH0A0HYM2 Oct 15 3.23 pct (3.25 Oct 14, 3.16 Oct 13, 3.11 Oct 12, 3.11 Oct 9) - credit is out of its 303-312 band to the wide side and up 12bp on the week, and FRED still has NOT posted an Oct 16 print, so the Friday equity rout is still not in the credit data. The Oct 16 reading, due today or tomorrow, is the one that matters. FRED NFCI week ending Oct 9 minus 0.499 (minus 0.507, minus 0.517, minus 0.527, minus 0.536) - a fifth week of tightening from a very loose base, drift not stress, and it pre-dates the selloff; the Oct 21 print is the first post-selloff read. FRED ICSA week ending Oct 10 199k (198k, 199k, 198k, 198k) - a fourth straight week below 200k, next release Oct 22. Labour is still the strongest tile on the board. VIX STILL UNCONFIRMED, FOURTH RUN: FRED VIXCLS has still not posted an Oct 16 close - its latest remains 16.46 (Oct 15), with 16.87 Oct 14, 15.27 Oct 13, 15.21 Oct 12, 14.84 Oct 9. The 21.41 value used here is wire-sourced with a consistent plus 4.97 delta off the official Oct 15 close and is carried for a fourth run. Worth noting the tension: AP reports the Friday session as S and P 500 minus 1.1 pct, Dow minus 0.3 pct, Nasdaq minus 2.1 pct, which is a bad day but not obviously a 30 pct VIX spike, and the old GitHub Action had served 19.99 for the same date. Treat 21.41 as approximately right and unconfirmed. If FRED posts Oct 16 today this resolves. FOMC - HOLD IS THE CONSENSUS, CONFIRMED INDEPENDENTLY: the Oct 27-28 meeting is priced at roughly 84-85 pct hold versus 15-16 pct hike (prediction markets and fed funds futures agree). The policy-error framing from the Oct 17 run stays retired. Fed funds target 3.75-4.00 pct. DOLLAR AND GROWTH PROXY: DXY 101.82 for Oct 19 (101.81 Oct 18, 101.84 Oct 16, 102.06 Oct 15, 102.55 Oct 14, 102.18 Oct 13) - down about 0.35 pct on the week and barely moved on the sanctions news; a dollar that will not rally on a hawkish CPI surprise remains the odd one out on this board. Growth proxy 1.57 (copper 6.57 USD/Lbs plus 0.54 pct and gold 4,181.16 USD/t.oz plus 0.35 pct, both Oct 19; 6.57/4181.16*1000 = 1.571) - fourth consecutive run identical at the second decimal, and notably copper is UP on an improving-supply-shock morning while gold also holds above 4,180, so neither metal is confirming a growth scare. Trend flat. REAL ECONOMY - ALL CARRIED, NOTHING NEW: consumer sentiment 46.3 (UMich preliminary October versus 47.8 expected and 48.1 final September, a five-month low, one-year inflation expectations 4.7 pct and five-year 3.5 pct, both up) trend down; ISM Manufacturing 54.5 (September, next Nov 2); building permits 1,403k (August - the September release lands TOMORROW Oct 20); LEI y/y minus 0.7 pct (September release Oct 22); Sahm Rule 0.00 (September, next Nov 6, trigger is plus 0.50). All flat. MONETARY PLUMBING - STILL BLIND, FOURTH RUN: the 3M SOFR-OIS spread was searched again (traditiondata, bluegamma, sofrrate, sofracademy, cbonds) and every free source serves the SOFR level or an OIS rate, never the spread, so 0bp is CARRIED AS A STANDING ASSUMPTION. The EUR/USD 3M cross-currency basis was also searched again including the CME XEURBI index page, which publishes a methodology and an empty end-of-day value field, so minus 10bp is also CARRIED AS AN ASSUMPTION. Global liquidity 1 (stable) is a judgement call, not a measurement - no balance-sheet regime change was found for the Fed, ECB, PBOC or BOJ. Two assumed tiles and one judgement tile out of eighteen, unchanged. INFRASTRUCTURE: git healthy, working tree clean at start, this scheduled session remains the sole writer of data.json (the GitHub Action stayed disabled since Oct 17), BDTI stayed removed. STILL OPEN FOR A FOURTH RUN - SECURITY: the origin remote is an HTTPS URL with a GitHub personal access token in plain text in .git/config. It is fine-grained and scoped to this repo, but it should be rotated and replaced with an SSH remote. Also still present: untracked junk in the repo root - _stale_git_locks/, _wtest, __pycache__/ and outputs/ - all safe to delete. PICTURE: for the first time in this episode the main driver is pointing the right way. The configuration is still risk-off - equity vol up about 44 pct on the week, credit broken out to the wide side, the curve at the flattest of the episode, consumer sentiment at a five-month low with rising inflation expectations - but the stagflationary half of the story depends on oil, and oil just took a policy-driven 2 USD hit with a credible Hormuz reopening on the table. Meanwhile the parts of the board that would confirm a recession are not confirming it: claims below 200k for a fourth week, copper up, 5y5y breakevens flat at 2.33, the curve steepening on the worst session, and the market pricing the Fed to sit still at roughly 85 pct. The honest read is an AI-valuation and credit unwind with an energy shock that has just begun to deflate, not a recession setup and not a policy error. The risk is that the oil relief is headline-deep: a waiver can be reversed and a mined tanker in Hormuz is a physical fact. WATCH, IN ORDER OF WEIGHT: whether Brent holds below 108 and whether the Hormuz deal is actually accepted (reopening would be the single biggest bullish repricing on this board); whether HY OAS keeps widening once the Oct 16 print lands; whether FRED confirms the Oct 16 VIX near 21.41 or nearer 20; whether 2s10s holds 35bp; the Oct 27-28 FOMC where a hike would be a genuine surprise; September building permits TOMORROW Oct 20, NFCI Oct 21 for the first post-selloff read, claims and September LEI Oct 22, EIA inventories Oct 21; rotating the embedded PAT.
